S.FORM: taavalaʔ-a maamia si tee=ku pu-a-iisua si-pu-ʔucipi=kani ʔənnaŋ si ni-i-vatu sua chiausou=maku iisi. sense=maku ni-ara-anai ara-caini, tokio ma-kaasi sian.
S.PHON: taavaɾaʔa maamia ʂi teeku puaiisua ʂipuʔutʂipikani ʔənnaŋ ʂi niivatu sua ʦhiausoumaku iiʂi sensemaku niaraanai araʦaini tokio makaaʂi ʂian
S.FORM: taavara'a maamia si teeku puaiisua sipu'ucipikani 'ennang si niivatu sua chiausoumaku iisi. sensemaku niaraanai aracaini, tokio makaasi sian.
S.PHON: taava[r|ɾ]aʔa maamia ʂi teeku puaiisua ʂipuʔutʂipikani ʔennaŋ ʂi niivatu sua ʦhiausoumaku iiʂi sensemaku nia[r|ɾ]aanai a[r|ɾ]aʦaini tokio makaaʂi ʂian
S.TRANSL: (I) only know that I will talk about how to cook the fruit of the bird lime plant because my professor came here from Tokyo far away.

S.FORM: tee=kirimi ʔikua, um-ala kaari=mita kari kanakanavu.
S.PHON: teekirimi ʔikua umaɾa kaarimita kari kanakanavu
S.FORM: teekirimi 'ikua, umara kaarimita kari kanakanavu.
S.PHON: teeki[r|ɾ]imi ʔikua uma[r|ɾ]a kaa[r|ɾ]imita ka[r|ɾ]i kanakanavu
S.TRANSL: He looked for me to record our Kanakanavu language.

S.FORM: nakai ʔuuna ni-i-vatu mii sauni pu-a-iisua ʔənnaŋ.
S.PHON: nakai ʔuuna niivatu mii sauni puaiisua ʔənnaŋ
S.FORM: nakai 'uuna niivatu mii sauni puaiisua 'ennang.
S.PHON: nakai ʔuuna niivatu mii sauni puaiisua ʔennaŋ
S.TRANSL: (I) just talked about how to cook the fruit of the bird lime plant.

S.FORM: tee=kani taa=ku taavalaʔ-ən sua si-pu-ʔucipi=kani ʔənnaŋ.
S.PHON: teekani taaku taavaɾaʔən sua ʂipuʔutʂipikani ʔənnaŋ
S.FORM: teekani taaku taavara'en sua sipu'ucipikani 'ennang.
S.PHON: teekani taaku taava[r|ɾ]aʔen sua ʂipuʔutʂipikani ʔennaŋ
S.TRANSL: It is said that he wants to learn how to cook the fruit of the bird lime plant.

S.FORM: tee=pa=ku masi-aŋaanai t<um>uturu, sua si-pu-ʔucipi ʔənnaŋ ia, ni-pa-kari=cu=maku misa-ən.
S.PHON: teepaku maʂiaŋaanai tumuturu sua ʂipuʔutʂipi ʔənnaŋ ia nipakariʦumaku misaən
S.FORM: teepaku masiangaanai t<um>uturu, sua sipu'ucipi 'ennang ia, nipakaricumaku misaen.
S.PHON: teepaku maʂiaŋaanai tumutu[r|ɾ]u sua ʂipuʔutʂipi ʔennaŋ ia nipaka[r|ɾ]iʦumaku misaen
S.TRANSL: As I have just said it, I will briefly talk about how to cook the fruit of the bird lime plant.

S.FORM: cu-culu mara-ʔapi-ʔaranasə kitana nu pu-ʔucipi=kita ʔənnaŋ.
S.PHON: ʦuʦuɾu maraʔapiʔaranasə kitana nu puʔutʂipikita ʔənnaŋ
S.FORM: cucuru mara'api'aranase kitana nu pu'ucipikita 'ennang.
S.PHON: ʦuʦu[r|ɾ]u ma[r|ɾ]aʔapiʔa[r|ɾ]anase kitana nu puʔutʂipikita ʔennaŋ
S.TRANSL: It is really a little troublesome for us when we cook it.

S.FORM: pu-ʔucipi ʔənnaŋ ia, apən-ən=pa, apən-ən=pa masi-palu-paluʔu.
S.PHON: puʔutʂipi ʔənnaŋ ia apənənpa apənənpa maʂipaɾupaɾuʔu
S.FORM: pu'ucipi 'ennang ia, apenenpa, apenenpa masiparuparu'u.
S.PHON: puʔutʂipi ʔennaŋ ia apenenpa apenenpa maʂipa[r|ɾ]upa[r|ɾ]uʔu
S.TRANSL: In order to cook the fruit of the bird lime plant, we have to pluck the fruits one by one and take them away.

S.FORM: nuu ni-apən-an=ci masi-palu-paluʔu ia, ari-sina-ən=cu na canumu.
S.PHON: nuu niapənantʂi maʂipaɾupaɾuʔu ia ariʂinaənʦu na ʦanumu
S.FORM: nuu niapenanci masiparuparu'u ia, arisinaencu na canumu.
S.PHON: nuu niapenantʂi maʂipa[r|ɾ]upa[r|ɾ]uʔu ia a[r|ɾ]iʂinaenʦu na ʦanumu
S.TRANSL: When we have plucked the fruit and taken it away, we wash it in water.

S.FORM: nu ni-ari-sina-n=ci ia, pu-ʔucip-in=cu na ʔuia.
S.PHON: nu niariʂinantʂi ia puʔutʂipinʦu na ʔuia
S.FORM: nu niarisinanci ia, pu'ucipincu na 'uia.
S.PHON: nu nia[r|ɾ]iʂinantʂi ia puʔutʂipinʦu na ʔuia
S.TRANSL: When it has been washed, we cook it in an iron pot.

S.FORM: nakai sua pu-ʔucipi ia, tia=saihu.
S.PHON: nakai sua puʔutʂipi ia tiasaihu
S.FORM: nakai sua pu'ucipi ia, tiasaihu.
S.PHON: nakai sua puʔutʂipi ia tiasaihu
S.TRANSL: But it takes a specialist to cook it.

S.FORM: nuu kaa=kia saihu pu-ʔucipi ia, tia=ma-pakacu, saauvu sauni.
S.PHON: nuu kaakia saihu puʔutʂipi ia tiamapakaʦu saauvu sauni
S.FORM: nuu kaakia saihu pu'ucipi ia, tiamapakacu, saauvu sauni.
S.PHON: nuu kaakia saihu puʔutʂipi ia tiamapakaʦu saauvu sauni
S.TRANSL: If it is not cooked by a specialist, it will taste astringent, but it smells (good) today.

S.FORM: sua iiku ia, masi-raru=cu=ku pu-ʔucipi nu pu-ʔucipi=kia ia, nu isəʔ-ən=ci na ʔuia ia, araanai=cu ʔinia t<um>a-tii-tiuru ma-kaasi na m-usu-cikiciki sua ʔənnaŋ.
S.PHON: sua iiku ia maʂiraruʦuku puʔutʂipi nu puʔutʂipikia ia nu isəʔəntʂi na ʔuia ia araanaiʦu ʔinia tumatiitiuru makaaʂi na musutʂikitʂiki sua ʔənnaŋ
S.FORM: sua iiku ia, masirarucuku pu'ucipi nu pu'ucipikia ia, nu ise'enci na 'uia ia, araanaicu 'inia t<um>atiitiuru makaasi na musucikiciki sua 'ennang.
S.PHON: sua iiku ia maʂi[r|ɾ]a[r|ɾ]uʦuku puʔutʂipi nu puʔutʂipikia ia nu iseʔentʂi na ʔuia ia a[r|ɾ]aanaiʦu ʔinia tumatiitiu[r|ɾ]u makaaʂi na musutʂikitʂiki sua ʔennaŋ
S.TRANSL: If I cook the fruit of the bird lime plant, I'll stir it in the pot until the water boils.

S.FORM: sua ʔənnaŋ nu ma-curu=ci ia, ʔuna=cu sauvu.
S.PHON: sua ʔənnaŋ nu maʦurutʂi ia ʔunaʦu sauvu
S.FORM: sua 'ennang nu macuruci ia, 'unacu sauvu.
S.PHON: sua ʔennaŋ nu maʦu[r|ɾ]utʂi ia ʔunaʦu sauvu
S.TRANSL: The fruit of the bird lime plant has a smell when it is cooked.

S.FORM: nu ʔuna=ci sauvu ia, taavalaʔə tanam-ən k<um>aən-a.
S.PHON: nu ʔunatʂi sauvu ia taavaɾaʔə tanamən kumaəna
S.FORM: nu 'unaci sauvu ia, taavara'e tanamen k<um>aena.
S.PHON: nu ʔunatʂi sauvu ia taava[r|ɾ]aʔe tanamen kumaena
S.TRANSL: When it has a smell, you may try to eat it.

S.FORM: kaʔan tia=kaʔan=pa haʔan-ən nuu ma-curu=ci ia, taavalaʔ-ən=cu.
S.PHON: kaʔan tiakaʔanpa haʔanən nuu maʦurutʂi ia taavaɾaʔənʦu
S.FORM: ka'an tiaka'anpa ha'anen nuu macuruci ia, taavara'encu.
S.PHON: kaʔan tiakaʔanpa haʔanen nuu maʦu[r|ɾ]utʂi ia taava[r|ɾ]aʔenʦu
S.TRANSL: Don't remove it yet (from the stove) when you know it is already cooked.

S.FORM: cəʔəra-ən=pa canum-ini tee=kara=cu tiʔiŋi, haʔan-ən sua kaʔan=kara=pa m-usu-pala-pala ʔinia maʔaini.
S.PHON: ʦəʔəraənpa ʦanumini teekaraʦu tiʔiŋi haʔanən sua kaʔankarapa musupaɾapaɾa ʔinia maʔaini
S.FORM: ce'eraenpa canumini teekaracu ti'ingi, ha'anen sua ka'ankarapa musuparapara 'inia ma'aini.
S.PHON: ʦeʔe[r|ɾ]aenpa ʦanumini teeka[r|ɾ]aʦu tiʔiŋi haʔanen sua kaʔanka[r|ɾ]apa musupa[r|ɾ]apa[r|ɾ]a ʔinia maʔaini
S.TRANSL: Check if there is only a little bit of water left, and then remove the pot from the stove. Then you can add salt to it until the water boils.

S.FORM: misai ia, taavalaʔə=ci=kia taka-cii-cini pa-cəpə-cəpəŋ nuu mia-ʔanan=ci ma-tatərəcaŋ=ci ia, valu-ən=cu mu-valu.
S.PHON: misai ia taavaɾaʔətʂikia takatʂiitʂini paʦəpəʦəpəŋ nuu miaʔanantʂi matatərəʦaŋtʂi ia vaɾuənʦu muvaɾu
S.FORM: misai ia, taavara'ecikia takaciicini pacepecepeng nuu mia'ananci mataterecangci ia, varuencu muvaru.
S.PHON: misai ia taava[r|ɾ]aʔetʂikia takatʂiitʂini paʦepeʦepeŋ nuu miaʔanantʂi matate[r|ɾ]eʦaŋtʂi ia va[r|ɾ]uenʦu muva[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: If so, we can consider putting it down and let it cool off and soften.

S.FORM: ma-valuu=ci lapati-ini ia, carəʔ-ən=cu. carəʔ-ən=ci ia, kaa-manəŋ-ən=cu kaa-ma-kakəaŋə na ʔuia.
S.PHON: mavaɾuutʂi ɾapatiini ia ʦarəʔənʦu ʦarəʔəntʂi ia kaamanəŋənʦu kaamakakəaŋə na ʔuia
S.FORM: mavaruuci rapatiini ia, care'encu. care'enci ia, kaamanengencu kaamakakeange na 'uia.
S.PHON: mava[r|ɾ]uutʂi [r|ɾ]apatiini ia ʦa[r|ɾ]eʔenʦu ʦa[r|ɾ]eʔentʂi ia kaamaneŋenʦu kaamakakeaŋe na ʔuia
S.TRANSL: If the rind of the fruit is softened, we can sprinkle salt on it. Then solidify it in an iron pot.

S.FORM: ma-tatərəcaŋ=ci ia, ciri-in=cu na taumarə. ciri-in na taumarə. kaa-manəŋ-ən=cu tee=ci kaa-manəŋ-ən ia, ma-ala=kia takupin tiʔiŋ-ai.
S.PHON: matatərəʦaŋtʂi ia tʂiriinʦu na taumarə tʂiriin na taumarə kaamanəŋənʦu teetʂi kaamanəŋən ia maaɾakia takupin tiʔiŋai
S.FORM: mataterecangci ia, ciriincu na taumare. ciriin na taumare. kaamanengencu teeci kaamanengen ia, maarakia takupin ti'ingai.
S.PHON: matate[r|ɾ]eʦaŋtʂi ia tʂi[r|ɾ]iinʦu na tauma[r|ɾ]e tʂi[r|ɾ]iin na tauma[r|ɾ]e kaamaneŋenʦu teetʂi kaamaneŋen ia maa[r|ɾ]akia takupin tiʔiŋai
S.TRANSL: When the fruit cools off, pour it into a winnowing basket. We can then work on it with a small bowl on the winnowing basket.

S.FORM: ari-kuuru maamia ma-kaasi, masi-kəpə na takupin. pasa-nairi=pa na taumarə.
S.PHON: arikuuru maamia makaaʂi maʂikəpə na takupin pasanairipa na taumarə
S.FORM: arikuuru maamia makaasi, masikepe na takupin. pasanairipa na taumare.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]ikuu[r|ɾ]u maamia makaaʂi maʂikepe na takupin pasanai[r|ɾ]ipa na tauma[r|ɾ]e
S.TRANSL: (We) pour it into a small bowl to form a round shape in the winnowing basket.

S.FORM: ma-tatərəcaŋ=ci ia, isəʔ-ən=cu na pauŋaana tiʔiŋ-ai. nuu manaʔi=pa isəʔ-ən canumu.
S.PHON: matatərəʦaŋtʂi ia isəʔənʦu na pauŋaana tiʔiŋai nuu manaʔipa isəʔən ʦanumu
S.FORM: mataterecangci ia, ise'encu na paungaana ti'ingai. nuu mana'ipa ise'en canumu.
S.PHON: matate[r|ɾ]eʦaŋtʂi ia iseʔenʦu na pauŋaana tiʔiŋai nuu manaʔipa iseʔen ʦanumu
S.TRANSL: When it cools off and is poured into a small jar, there's no need to add water yet.

S.FORM: tanam-ən nu carəʔ-ən=ci ia, tanam-ən.
S.PHON: tanamən nu ʦarəʔəntʂi ia tanamən
S.FORM: tanamen nu care'enci ia, tanamen.
S.PHON: tanamen nu ʦa[r|ɾ]eʔentʂi ia tanamen
S.TRANSL: If (you) sprinkle salt on it, try to taste it.

S.FORM: nakai c<um>arəʔə=kamu ʔinia ia, ʔakun sua əm-əsəʔə ajinomoto aaka nu isəʔ-ən-ni.
S.PHON: nakai ʦumarəʔəkamu ʔinia ia ʔakun sua əməsəʔə ajinomoto aaka nu isəʔənni
S.FORM: nakai c<um>are'ekamu 'inia ia, 'akun sua emese'e ajinomoto aaka nu ise'enni.
S.PHON: nakai ʦuma[r|ɾ]eʔekamu ʔinia ia ʔakun sua emeseʔe ajinomoto aaka nu iseʔenni
S.TRANSL: If you sprinkle salt on it, don't add seasoning powder, which will spoil it.

S.FORM: isəʔ-ən=ci ajinomoto ia, um-ala=kia u-cani um-aŋəarə ia, isəʔ-ən=cu ajinomoto.
S.PHON: isəʔəntʂi ajinomoto ia umaɾakia uʦani umaŋəarə ia isəʔənʦu ajinomoto
S.FORM: ise'enci ajinomoto ia, umarakia ucani umangeare ia, ise'encu ajinomoto.
S.PHON: iseʔentʂi ajinomoto ia uma[r|ɾ]akia uʦani umaŋea[r|ɾ]e ia iseʔenʦu ajinomoto
S.TRANSL: If we add seasoning powder to it, we take one (fruit) and put in some seasoning powder to stir and fry it in a wok of oil.

S.FORM: pu-ʔucipi=kia ʔənnaŋ ia, "cu-cculu icibaŋ, icibaŋ" kisa-ən.
S.PHON: puʔutʂipikia ʔənnaŋ ia ʦuʦʦuɾu itʂi*aŋ itʂi*aŋ kisaən
S.FORM: pu'ucipikia 'ennang ia, "cuccuru icibang, icibang" kisaen.
S.PHON: puʔutʂipikia ʔennaŋ ia ʦuʦʦu[r|ɾ]u itʂi*aŋ itʂi*aŋ kisaen
S.TRANSL: When we cook the fruit of the bird lime plant, "It really tastes the best," it is said.

S.FORM: makasua sua si-a-tuuturu=maku kamua si-pu-ʔucipi ʔənnaŋ.
S.PHON: makasua sua ʂiatuuturumaku kamua ʂipuʔutʂipi ʔənnaŋ
S.FORM: makasua sua siatuuturumaku kamua sipu'ucipi 'ennang.
S.PHON: makasua sua ʂiatuutu[r|ɾ]umaku kamua ʂipuʔutʂipi ʔennaŋ
S.TRANSL: In that way, I'm teaching you how to cook the fruit of the bird lime plant.
